{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team / business owner  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — issues, walk-away items and next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the MSA against the playbook. The risk profile is sharply split.

**What is already good.** The protective, Vendor-facing terms are strong and need no redlining. Limitation of liability (§21) is mutual and sits at our preferred position, with a substantive cap base and the full carve-out set. Assignment and change of control (§24) is asymmetric in our favour. The licence grant (§13), performance warranties (§19), Vendor insurance (§18), audit rights against us (§22), and the auto-renewal/uplift mechanic (§8.2–8.3) all meet the preferred position. There are no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

**What is not acceptable.** The commercial-restraint and exit architecture of the agreement is the problem, and several items land in playbook walk-away territory:

- **No indemnification article exists at all.** The outline jumps from §19 to §21, yet §9.3, §19.4, §21.3 and §30.5 all cross-reference indemnities that are not in the document (including a broken reference to "Section 20.5"). We have no Vendor IP indemnity.
- **Three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay (§2.1), expressly "without reduction or termination rights"**, with **no termination for convenience anywhere in §9**. We are locked into USD 6,000,000 of spend with no exit.
- **§7.2 imposes a disclose-and-match obligation on us** before we may engage another provider — a de facto exclusivity and MFN burden on the Customer, unlimited as to product, term and comparison method.
- **Duplicate-numbered §12.4 contains a 24-month post-term non-compete and a one-way 24-month no-hire** on us, with the general-advertising carve-out expressly negated.
- **No post-termination transition assistance and no obligation to return or delete Customer Data.** §16.5 carves Customer Data out of the return/destroy duty and defers to a "Section 11" that does not exist in the document.
- **§14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable built for us**, with only a revocable, term-limited licence back.
- **§28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts**, outside the accepted list and in direct conflict with §28.2, which gives exclusive jurisdiction to the New York County courts.

A notable pattern supports our position in negotiation: §12.3 records Vendor's own acknowledgement that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." That clause directly contradicts §2.1, §7.2 and both §12.4 provisions. We should press these as internal drafting inconsistencies to be conformed to §12.3, not as new asks.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposed action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | §14.2 (with §13.2, §13.3, §14.3) | Vendor owns every Deliverable; our licence is revocable and term-limited. Fails preferred and fallback. Flip ownership to Customer with assignment on creation; Vendor retains Vendor Technology under §14.3. |
| 2 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | §10 (§10.2); §16.5 | No transition-assistance duty and no data return/export or certified deletion. Insert new §10.3: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable export within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| 3 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No §20; cross-referenced at §9.3, §19.4, §21.3, §30.5 | Walk-away. Insert §20: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches, gross negligence/wilful misconduct; procure/modify/replace/refund remedies at §20.5 (restoring the §9.3 cross-reference); narrow reciprocal Customer indemnity. |
| 4 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §9 (§9.3); §8.1; §2.1 | Walk-away. No convenience right in a three-year term. Insert §9.4: Customer termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term; conforming edit to §2.1. |
| 5 | Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | §2.1 (cf. §12.3) | Walk-away. Three-year USD 2,000,000 p.a. take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". Delete; Fees payable only for Services ordered or used. Fallback: single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, settled by true-up. |
| 6 | Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 (cf. §12.3) | Walk-away. Open-ended obligation to disclose and match any better third-party offer, unlimited as to product, term and comparison method. Delete the obligation. |
| 7 | Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 (cf. §12.3) | Same clause, independent breach: the disclose-and-match precondition restrains our sourcing freedom for the full term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit. Resolved by the single deletion at item 6. |
| 8 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (competitive activity) (cf. §12.3) | Walk-away. 24-month post-term, any product, any territory, no carve-outs. Delete, leaving §12.3 to govern. Fallback: term-only restriction on a single named product. |
| 9 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (no-hire) (cf. §12.3) | Walk-away. One-way 24-month outright no-hire covering all Vendor employees, with general-advertising/unsolicited-application carve-out expressly negated. Delete. Fallback: mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services, with standard carve-outs. |
| 10 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | §28.1 (cf. §28.2) | Walk-away (exclusive foreign venue outside the accepted list) and internally inconsistent with §28.2. Change §28.1 to New York law and the New York County courts; align the §28.2 injunction carve-out. §28.3 escalation is acceptable as drafted. |
| 11 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | §21.1–21.4; §1.5; §18.2 | Preferred position: mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, substantive Fee base, full carve-out set. No redline. |
| 12 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §24.1–24.4; §13.3 | Preferred position; asymmetric in our favour (no Vendor repricing, acceleration or termination on our change of control). No redline. |
| 13 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | §27.3; §7.3; §24.4 | No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or minimum termination charge. The §2.1 take-or-pay is addressed at item 5 and not double-flagged. No redline. |
| 14 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | §13.1–13.3; §14.3; §10.1 | Preferred position: Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users covered; paid-up perpetual rights to Vendor Technology. The §14.2 "revocable" wording is addressed as an ownership issue at item 1. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §22.1–22.3 | Preferred position: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, no system/third-party data access, Vendor bears cost below a 5% underpayment threshold. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | §8.2–8.3 | Preferred position: 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension if missed; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | §19.1–19.5; §6.2 | Preferred position and better: hosted-service conformity for the whole subscription term, full remedy ladder, mutual and carved-back disclaimer. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §18.1–18.2 | Preferred position: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp, term plus one year; insurance does not cap liability. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in playbook walk-away territory. We should not sign without resolution on each:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing §20).** No IP infringement defence at all, and multiple clauses in the agreement already assume one exists.
2. **§2.1 take-or-pay** — three years at USD 2,000,000 p.a., expressly without reduction or termination rights.
3. **No termination for convenience (§9)** — a three-year term with no Customer exit, compounding item 2.
4. **§7.2 disclose-and-match** — open-ended MFN and de facto exclusivity binding the Customer.
5. **§12.4 non-compete** — 24 months post-term, any product, any territory, no carve-outs.
6. **§12.4 no-hire** — one-way, 24 months, all employees, carve-outs expressly negated.
7. **§28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts** — outside the accepted list and contradicted by §28.2.

Items 4, 5 and 6 are each contradicted by Vendor's own acknowledgement in **§12.3**; item 7 is contradicted by **§28.2**. These should be framed to Vendor as conforming corrections.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering items 1–10 in the table. Proposed positions and fallbacks are already drafted for each.
2. **Manual drafting attention required.** Automated verification of the proposed edits did not land cleanly for the following, which need counsel to draft and re-verify before the turn goes out: **§14.2 deliverable ownership**, **new §10.3 transition and data return**, **§7.2 MFN deletion**, **§2.1 minimum commitment deletion**, and **§12.4 no-hire deletion**. The edits to §7.2 (exclusivity), §28.1 (governing law), §12.4 (non-compete), new §20 (indemnity) and new §9.4 (termination for convenience) verified after repair and can be sent as drafted.
3. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the walk-away items as a single package, opening on the internal inconsistencies (§12.3 and §28.2) where Vendor's own drafting supports us. Treat the deliverable-ownership and transition/data-return items as the next tier.
4. **Coordinate one edit to §7.2.** A single deletion clears both the MFN and exclusivity findings; we should not present them as two separate asks.
5. **Confirm the cross-reference clean-up.** Inserting §20 restores the broken §9.3 reference to "Section 20.5"; §16.5's reference to a non-existent "Section 11" should be repointed to the new §10.3.
6. **Business input needed** on (a) whether any volume commitment is commercially acceptable and, if so, whether the 12-month reducible fallback works; and (b) the service-level exhibit referenced at §2.2, which is not in the body and has not been reviewed — please circulate it so we can assess service credits and the §9.3 "repeatedly misses a critical service level" trigger."}
